cards.explanation: The answer is his share of the estate. The younger son walks up and says, “Father, give me my share of the estate.” That's the whole ask. I think that's a bold thing to say to your own father, friends. And the father hears it and divides his property between his sons.
The answer is False. The father doesn't refuse. The text says he divided his property between both sons. The younger son asked, and the younger son got it.
The word is squandered, friends. The younger son squandered his wealth in wild living. It means he spent what he had wastefully. It's the opposite of me guarding the last chocolate chip in the bowl.

The answer is into his fields to feed the pigs. Pigs, friends. A son who started with a share of the estate is now working for a citizen of that country. I think that's a long way down from where he started.
The answer is False. No one gives him food. The text says “…no one would give him a thing.” He's hungry enough to long for what the pigs are eating.

The answer is father. The younger son says, “How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food, but here I am, starving to death!” Even the hired servants back home are eating well. That's when he starts turning toward home.

The answer is like one of his hired servants. He means to say, “Make me like one of your hired servants.” He's already decided he's no longer worthy to be called a son. I think he's trying to ask for as little as he can.

The answer is that the father runs to him and embraces him. The text says the father saw him while he was still in the distance, “He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.” I'd run too, but on my gold base it's more of a hop. No waiting around, friends.

The word is compassion. The text says his father saw him and “…was filled with compassion.” And that's before the son says one word of his speech. The first thing the son meets is the father running toward him.

The reason is that his son was dead and is alive again. The father says, “For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!” Notice he doesn't mention the money or any list of conditions. The celebration is about his son being back.
The answer is False. The older son doesn't head straight inside. He calls one of the servants and asks what was going on. He hears a party before he knows what it's for.
The answer is True. The text says, “The older son became angry and refused to go in.” He's standing outside while the party goes on without him. I think that's a tough spot for his father too.
The word is pleads. The father came out and pleaded with him. The older son refused to go in, so the father comes out to him.

The answer is False. The older son says, “…when this son of yours returns…” He doesn't call him my brother. The father is the one who says, “…this brother of yours was dead and is alive again…” (Luke 15:32).

The answer is that everything the father has is his. The father says, “Son, you are always with me… and all that is mine is yours.” Look at how he starts, with the word son. All that is the father's, he says, is the older son's.
The word is brother. The father says, “…this brother of yours was dead and is alive again…” He gives the older son back the word he left out. The younger one is still his brother.
